info.bio: Robert Fripp (n. 16 de mayo de 1946), es uno de los guitarristas que más ha influenciado al sonido del rock progresivo, sinfónico y todas sus variantes desde finales de los años '60. Nació en Bear Cross, Inglaterra. Aprendió a tocar la guitarra a los 11 años. Luego de participar en varias bandas desde los 14 años, se convierte a finales de los '60 en uno de los fundadores del género progresivo junto a King Crimson. Es también famoso por su singular técnica llamada ¨frippertronics¨.

scenes.name: Rock progresivo
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Al emigrar a Gran Bretaña, el rock se convierte en mercancía de moda pero también se descontextualiza: lo que en EE UU era el diario de la juventud se vuelve en Gran Bretaña un ensayo. El progresivo no comenta la cultura juvenil sino que busca la innovación técnica: arranca con las óperas rock (S.F. Sorrow, Tommy) y los álbumes conceptuales, lo cimentan Traffic, Jeff Beck, Jethro Tull, Family y Genesis, y alcanza su cima con King Crimson (In The Court Of The Crimson King), Van Der Graaf Generator y Yes. Colosseum, la Third Ear Band (inventores de la world music), las variantes góticas (High Tide, Black Widow) y folk (Comus, Strawbs), Gentle Giant, Emerson Lake & Palmer y Roxy Music, que revoluciona el género y prepara la new wave y el synth-pop.

podcast.title: Contribution to Heroes (1977)
podcast.body: Robert Fripp was invited by Brian Eno to Berlin to record guitar parts for David Bowie's "Heroes." Fripp was initially hesitant, acknowledging that he hadn't played a guitar in years and was unsure how it would turn out, especially since King Crimson was not actively working or performing concerts at that time. Despite his reservations, he traveled to Berlin at Eno's insistence and recorded for the album.

podcast.title: Feedback Loops for David Bowie (1977)
podcast.body: In 1977, Robert Fripp was brought in to collaborate with David Bowie for his "Heroes" album in Berlin, with the sole instruction to "do something weird" for the title track. Fripp created three distinct feedback loops: an A note fed back four feet from the amplifier, a G note fed back three feet from the amp, and a similar third take. All these guitar feedback tracks were then processed through an EMS synthesizer, a keyboard-less synth about the size of a briefcase, contributing a unique distorted and feedback-laden texture to Bowie's song. "Three takes, all based on feedback loops."

podcast.title: Windows Vista Startup Sound (2007)
podcast.body: Robert Fripp, the renowned guitarist of King Crimson and a friend and collaborator of Brian Eno, was responsible for creating the startup sound for Microsoft's Windows Vista operating system. This continued the tradition of established musicians composing these iconic computer audio cues. "el de Windows Vista, creado también por otro músico reputado, por cierto, Robert Fripp, guitaristare, King Crimson y amigo y colaborador de Inno."

srcs.episode: Por Qué Tu Cerebro Nunca Olvidará Este Sonido

podcast.title: Anger Over Kanye West Sampling (2012-2013)
podcast.body: Robert Fripp expressed immense anger ("very, very angry") after discovering in 2012, through the press and a YouTube video, that Kanye West had sampled the first track from King Crimson's first album in his 2010 song "Power" without prior permission. His fury was heightened by Universal Music (owner of both Island Records and Kanye West's label) effectively granting itself permission without notifying him. "Robert Flip no lo avisara le cabrió muchísimo se cabrió muchísimo pero muchísimo tenemos entrevistas del 2013 y 2012 cabreadísimo."

podcast.title: Continued Legal Battles with Universal Music (Post-2012)
podcast.body: Following the Kanye West sampling incident, Robert Fripp initiated "another very expensive and very long process" of lawsuits against Universal Music, which commenced in 2012 and continued for years. "empezó otro carísimo y larguísimo proceso desde 2012 con Universal Music."

podcast.title: Exhaustion and Temporary Retirement Announcement (2015)
podcast.body: In a 2015 interview with the Financial Times, Robert Fripp publicly stated his intention to leave music, citing fatigue from constantly defending his rights instead of dedicating his time to composing or playing. However, this declaration proved to be temporary, as he remained active and had a tour planned for 2018. "en el Finance Al Time a Robert Flip que dice que él deja la música porque está fatigado y que por desgracia en vez de dedicar esa componería a tocar es la lo único que se dedica a perseguir la defensa de los derechos de su material."

podcast.title: Absence from David Bowie's *Lodger*
podcast.body: Robert Fripp was not involved in the recording of David Bowie's *Lodger* album; his place was taken by Adrian Belew, who would also later become a member of King Crimson. "Esta vez Robert Thrip no estaría involucrado en la grabación, su lugar lo ocuparía, casualmente, otro futuro King Crimson, Adrián Beléu."

podcast.title: Berlin Collaborator
podcast.body: Robert Fripp, a prominent figure from King Crimson, made multiple trips to Germany to contribute his guitar work to the recording sessions associated with the "Berlin Trilogy" projects. His involvement highlights the wider network of musicians contributing to this creative period. "Me refiero Robert Fripp y Día Alemania varias veces ayudarlos a grabar con sus guitarras."

srcs.episode: David Bowie: La trilogía de Berlin 1

podcast.title: Co-Ownership and Shared Rights Management
podcast.body: Despite successfully recovering a significant portion of King Crimson's material rights, Robert Fripp is not the sole owner. He is legally obligated to share the management of these rights with other former members of King Crimson and Island Records, even for material he did not personally create. "está obligado a compartir esta gestión de derechos con otros miembros que han pasado por la carrera de King Crimson y por Islan Records."

podcast.title: Complex Rights Management After Greg Lake's Death
podcast.body: The complexities of managing King Crimson's rights intensified significantly after Greg Lake's death from cancer a few years prior. Lake was regarded as the "true genius" behind the band's first album, the rights for which Robert Fripp had largely managed almost single-handedly. "esta situación se hizo bastante complicado tras la muerte hace unos años de Greg Lake por un cáncer cuando él había sido el verdadero genio que estaba detrás del primer disco de King Crimson."

podcast.title: Contribution to David Bowie's *Heroes*
podcast.body: Robert Fripp, of King Crimson, joined the recording sessions for David Bowie's *Heroes*. He surprised Bowie and Visconti with his enthusiasm and adaptability to the songs, helping to define the epic, striking atmosphere of the title track "Heroes" and contributing unique and experimental sound textures. "Robert Fry, quien sorprendió Bowie a Visconti por subir tu asismo y su forma de adaptarse a las canciones en las que estaba trabajando. Ayuda a definir la atmósfera épica llamativa de Heroes, la canción homonima, también participó con la creación de texturas sonoras únicas y experimentales."

podcast.title: Current Negotiations with Spotify
podcast.body: Robert Fripp (representing King Crimson) has been engaged in discussions with Spotify for several years concerning the inclusion of the band's discography on the platform. Despite ongoing negotiations, an agreement has not yet been reached, though the dialogue suggests a potential future resolution, possibly on financial terms. "Robert Flip está en conversaciones con Spotify y Spotify al menos ha admitido que está en conversaciones con King Crimson desde hace años para intentar tener su discográfica pero no están llegando a un acuerdo."

podcast.title: Decades-Long Fight for Rights Recovery (1990s)
podcast.body: Robert Fripp engaged in a "huge process of legal disputes" throughout almost the entire 1990s. He fought distributors, Island Records, and even former King Crimson members to reclaim the rights to King Crimson's material, a "complex and very expensive process of lawyers" from which he eventually recovered everything. "durante casi toda la década de los 90 es un complejísimo y carísimo proceso de abogados para recuperar su material y lo consigue recuperar todo."

podcast.title: Disagreement with Greg Lake on Sampling
podcast.body: Robert Fripp's frustration regarding the Kanye West sampling was compounded by Greg Lake's positive reaction. Lake, whom Fripp considered the "true composer" and "true genius" of that particular part and album, found the sampling a "fantastic idea" and felt "truly flattered" that a significant artist for younger generations like Kanye West would incorporate his composed material. "lo que más le cabrió fue que Greg Lake... le parece una idea fantástica."

podcast.title: Founding Discipline Global Mobile (Late 1980s)
podcast.body: In the late 1980s, Robert Fripp founded his own record label, Discipline Global Mobile (DGM), after realizing that Island Records held more rights to his material than he did. This decision was a direct response to perceived fraud and a common issue faced by many artists of that era. "decide fundar su propia discográfica Discipline Mobile no Discipline Global Mobile, sí era esa."

podcast.title: Legal Action Against Grooveshark
podcast.body: Robert Fripp launched a major legal process against Grooveshark, a streaming service described as a "pre-Spotify." This dispute became highly controversial, with Fripp's private emails threatening Grooveshark executives being publicly published. Fripp was recognized as a key figure in the platform's eventual closure. "Robert Flip contra Groofshark."

podcast.title: Legal Dispute with Universal Music Corporate (2000s)
podcast.body: Robert Fripp initiated another "huge process of lawsuits" against Universal Music Corporate after they acquired Island Records. Universal began publishing King Crimson compilations, re-editions, and unreleased material found in Island Records' archives without Fripp's consent, despite Fripp having believed his legal processes were concluded. "empieza a ver un enorme problema cuando ya Robert Flip creía que había acabado todos sus procesos legales porque Universal Music Corporate empieza a publicar una serie de recopilatorios de red ediciones e incluso de cierto material inédito que había quedado en las suficinas de Islan Records sin el consentimiento de Robert Flip."

podcast.title: Pioneering Legal Battles for Rights
podcast.body: Robert Fripp's complex and lengthy legal battles against the music industry, particularly concerning King Crimson's catalog, have been instrumental in establishing new jurisprudential bases for understanding and managing musical rights. His personal struggle has significantly influenced how rights management is perceived today. "los procesos judiciales de King Crimson o de Robert Flip en concreto. En contra de la industria musical, han sentado muchas bases de cómo entendemos la gestión de derechos."

podcast.title: Significant Legal Victories and Industry Precedents
podcast.body: Robert Fripp achieved "enormous victories" in his protracted legal battles, successfully recovering rights he had previously lost. His efforts established "important precedents for the industry," significantly smoothing the path for many artists from the 1960s and 1970s, such as AC/DC, who had also been divested of their rights by record labels. "ha conseguido enormes victorias porque no solo recuperó todos los derechos que no tenía de King Crimson pero también esentaba precedentes importantes para la industria se facilitó mucho el camino para muchos artistas que durante los años 60 y 70 habían perdido sus derechos a manos de discográficas como el caso de Isidisi o de muchas otras."
